https://sl.china-embassy.gov.cn/eng/zgyw.text: Home About the Embassy China-Sierra Leone Relations Consular Service Services Topics On July 23, 2026, Chairman of the Standing Committee of the National Peopleâs Congress (NPC) Zhao Leji held talks with Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies of the Parliament of the Czech Republic Tomio Okamura at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Zhao Leji noted that maintaining and developing China-Czech relations serves the fundamental and long-term interests of both countries and meets the shared aspirations of the two peoples. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Czech strategic partnership. China is ready to work with the Czech side to carry forward traditional friendship, enhance mutual understanding and trust, strengthen exchanges and cooperation, and promote the sound and steady growth of China-Czech relations. Zhao Leji pointed out that China highly appreciates the positive and pragmatic policy toward China adopted by the new Czech government and the Chamber of Deputies of the Parliament. Both sides should cement the political foundation of their relations, consolidate the momentum of improvement in bilateral relations, and resume and strengthen exchanges and interactions at all levels and across all fields. Efforts should be made to further tap into cooperation potential, give full play to the role of mechanisms such as the China-Czech Joint Ministerial Economic Committee and the China-CEEC Expo, explore ways to strengthen cooperation in fields including new energy and electric vehicles, and support enterprises of the two countries in expanding investment cooperation. The two sides should deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, expand cooperation in education, culture, science and technology, tourism, and at the sub-national level, encourage people of the two countries, especially the younger generation, to increase exchanges, and promote mutual understanding between the two peoples. They should also strengthen coordination and cooperation in international affairs, practice true multilateralism, safeguard the multilateral trading system and the stability and unimpeded flow of industrial and supply chains, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Zhao Leji stressed that exchanges between legislative bodies form an important part of the China-Czech strategic partnership. The NPC of China is ready to strengthen friendly exchanges with the Chamber of Deputies of the Parliament of the Czech Republic, carry out exchanges and mutual learning on legislation, oversight, economic development and improving peopleâs livelihoods, formulate, amend and adopt legal documents conducive to bilateral cooperation, and maintain close communication and coordination within multilateral mechanisms such as the Inter-Parliamentary Union. More Czech deputies are welcome to visit China. Zhao Leji noted that President Xi Jinping delivered a keynote address at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference, expounding Chinaâs positions and propositions, and announcing a series of measures to further support global AI development and advance global AI capacity building. China is ready to work with all countries, including the Czech Republic, to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in related fields, and promote the establishment of a fair and equitable global governance system for AI. Tomio Okamura stated that the 10th anniversary of the Czech-China strategic partnership holds special significance for the two countries, and he expressed the belief that on this solid foundation, the bilateral relations will continue to move forward. The Czech Republic adheres to the one-China policy. He expressed the hope to strengthen tourism cooperation with China, welcoming more Chinese tourists to visit the Czech Republic; expand cooperation in such areas as the economy and trade, cultural relic exhibitions, and direct flights; and enhance people-to-people and cultural exchanges. The Chamber of Deputies of the Parliament of the Czech Republic is ready to strengthen friendly exchanges with the NPC of China to enhance the friendship between the two peoples. Zheng Jianbang participated in the talks. http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/21/irans.text: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Friday it was time to end the months-long war with the United States because Tehran was in a position of strength over Washington."It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity," Pezeshkian said."The whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasises that America has attacked our schools, hospitals and infrastructure in violation of all regulations and is hated around the world."Iran's foreign ministry earlier accused the US of "economic terrorism" and "crimes against humanity" after Washington said it would ramp up sanctions to heap pressure on Tehran."The perpetrators and instigators of these sanctions are deserving of trial and punishment for committing such heinous crimes," it said in a statement carried by state media.Other senior Iranian officials also criticised the US sanctions plan."The so-called 'Economic D-Day' is a diversion from America's own crisis: unprecedented debt & surging interest costs," Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a post on X.Talks between the two remain on hold, with both sides in the war started by the US and Israel in late February locked in a stalemate.Tehran is keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington is persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.Beijing calls for 'responsible measures'Washington had urged other governments including China to join efforts to isolate the Iranian economy.Asked about US President Donald Trump's threats, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told reporters on Friday that "sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue"."China calls on all relevant parties to take responsible measures and resolve the problem through political and diplomatic means," he said.Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to visit the White House on 24 September when the topic of Iran is sure to come up, as it did when Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit in May.US Treasury chief Scott Bessent said the plan to ramp up economic sanctions against Iran meant Washington was less likely to have to return to heavy military operations against the country.Bessent said he would provide further details on the economic measures against Iran at a press conference on Monday.Economic pain, political pressureIran has been subject to Western sanctions for years and has become deft at partially circumventing them.It has expanded domestic production, used informal cross-border trade networks, bought restricted goods through third countries, and used a shadow fleet to transport its oil.“Iran’s resistance capacity not only avoids collapse, it also prevents the economic pain from translating into the political pressure and changes that the US expects,” said Hadi Kahalzadeh, an expert on Iran’s economy at Brandeis University.Yet inflation in Iran is expected to rise nearly 70% by the end of the year, according to the International Monetary Fund, and the country's economy is forecast to shrink by more than 5%.While petrol has remained cheap thanks to government subsidies, that may not last forever as supplies tighten.A presidential aide told Iranian state television last week that the country now uses more petrol each day than it produces and that Tehran might need to raise prices — something that has led to widespread protests in the past.Amid the economic struggles, Pezeshkian has said his government favours a negotiated end to the war.“What concerns us is people’s livelihoods and their economic situation, and we are doing everything we can to deal with it,” he told reporters last week.But the most powerful force in Iran remains the elite paramilitary IRGC, which has only become stronger after withstanding US and Israeli airstrikes that killed Iran’s top leaders during the war's opening salvos.The IRGC is pressing for greater concessions from the US, including Iranian control over Hormuz and financial compensation for the war.With negotiations to end the war stalled, Iran’s hardliners believe their country can endure the economic pressures longer than their adversaries.Iran’s Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei this month appointed a former IRGC commander to head Iran’s powerful Supreme National Security Council, a sign that he favours the hard-line approach.

https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.text: Leaders in the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam have expressed opposition to US plans to auction deep sea mining leases. Photograph: Amazing Aerial/Alamy View image in fullscreen Leaders in the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam have expressed opposition to US plans to auction deep sea mining leases. Photograph: Amazing Aerial/Alamy Deep-sea mining US territories hit out at Trump plan to explore deep sea mining in the Pacific US agency releases plan to lease millions of hectares of seabed off the coast of the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam Mar-Vic Cagurangan in Hagatna, Guam Sun 23 Aug 2026 21.34 EDT Last modified on Sun 23 Aug 2026 21.36 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A US government plan to lease out millions of hectares of seabed near the Mariana Trench for deep sea exploration has drawn opposition from US territories in the Pacific, as the Trump administration remains locked in a race with China for control of critical ocean minerals. On Tuesday, the Marine Mineral Administration (MMA), an agency under the US department of the interior, released a proposal to auction deep sea mining leases for 28m hectares (69m acres) of seafloor off the coast of the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam . ‘Severe’ stress on oceans as rate of sea level rise doubles in 10 years, UN warns Read more The leases ​would allow companies to ‌explore the seabed and potentially extract ‌deposits of critical minerals – known as polymetallic nodules – that could be used in batteries, electronics and defence technologies. Many environmental ​groups have ​opposed deep sea mining, arguing that more research is needed on its effects on marine ecosystems. The Northern Mariana Islands is a self-governing commonwealth of the United States, while Guam is an unincorporated territory of the US. The governor of the Northern Marianas, David Apatang, has said his government would approach the Trump administration’s proposal “with extreme caution”. Proposed lease area Apatang, while acknowledging the strategic importance of critical minerals, said it was necessary that “no activity, survey or otherwise, takes place without rigorous scientific baseline studies, complete transparency, and explicit protections for our marine resources”. He said his administration would “thoroughly examine the proposed terms over the next 60 days to ensure that the ecological integrity of our waters and the long-term wellbeing of the [Northern Marianas] are fully safeguarded”. The Guardian approached the Marine Mineral Administration for comment. In an earlier statement, the MMA said it had completed an environmental review of proposed commercial leases for critical minerals in the Marianas area. The MMA said it would consider comments from the governor. A statement from the office of the governor of Guam acknowledged the Trump administration’s focus on national security and strategic needs, but added: “National security cannot mean asking the people of the Pacific to accept environmental risks before those risks are fully understood. “We’re unequivocally opposed to the deep sea mining efforts in this region,” said Guam’s lieutenant governor, Joshua Tenorio. He told the Guardian: “The department of interior is giving assurances that mining activity is not going to commence with the awarding of these licences, [but] I think that this is a matter where we can’t really trust that because this has been rapidly evolving.” The proposed lease notice for deep sea exploration in the Marianas region came just weeks after the initiation of a leasing process for 12.4m hectares (31m acres) of American Samoa’s seafloor, with plans to award contracts in November. View image in fullscreen Donald Trump holds up a gold replica of a deep sea nodule given to him at a mining industry event earlier this month. Photograph: Eric Lee/Getty Images The governor of American Samoa, Nikolau Pula, said his government remained opposed to deep sea mining, noting that untested extraction processes could harm the territory’s tuna industry, which fuels its economy. On 19 August, environmental groups in American Samoa and Hawaii launched legal proceedings against the US government to halt the proposed auction of seafloor permits around the islands, alleging that federal agencies failed to evaluate the destructive impact mineral extractions could have on marine ecosystems. In a Hawaii court, Fa’asao Ameika Samoa and the Conservation Council for Hawaii warned that the extraction machinery “can destroy nearly all life in its path” and “stirs up sediments that can introduce toxic substances into the food web and smother seafloor ecosystems”. “Even just exploring for seabed minerals introduces extremely loud noise into the marine environment that can harm marine mammals and other wildlife,” the complaint reads. The Marine Mineral Administration was approached about the concerns over the American Samoa leasing process. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Sulaiman (left) and Kasim Khan say they have not been allowed to speak to their father for more than six months. Photograph: Vicki Couchman/The Times/News Licensing View image in fullscreen Sulaiman (left) and Kasim Khan say they have not been allowed to speak to their father for more than six months. Photograph: Vicki Couchman/The Times/News Licensing Imran Khan Imran Khan’s sons accuse Pakistani army chief of vendetta against imprisoned father Kasim and Sulaiman Khan tell Guardian they believe ex-PM is being ‘slowly killed’ by harsh treatment, driven by Asim Munir Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi and Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad Tue 15 Sep 2026 07.23 EDT Last modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 11.07 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions. Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, have become strong advocates for the release of their father, who has been held in Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023, and is serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges . They have not been allowed to speak to Khan for more than six months and have been prevented from travelling from the UK to Pakistan to lobby for his release. On Wednesday, the supreme court will rule on a case alleging the Pakistan government has been in contempt of court by denying Khan private hospital treatment for a worsening eye condition and preventing family from visiting him or speaking with him in jail for more than six months, in violation of a court order. Khan is being held in solitary confinement, in a cell alleged to be 6ft by 8ft. View image in fullscreen Imran Khan outside court in Lahore after a hearing in February 2023. Photograph: Mohsin Raza/Reuters Later this month, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) – the political party Khan founded in 1996, four years after retiring from international cricket – is planning a nationwide march demanding his release. Speaking to the Guardian from London, Khan’s sons – from his first marriage to Jemima Goldsmith – said they were “deeply, deeply concerned” about their father’s health, and that the conditions he was being kept in amounted to “a form of mental and physical torture”. “The reality is that he is locked in a tiny 6x8ft cell without human contact,” said Sulaiman. “He hasn’t been allowed new books for months and he’s not been allowed to see or speak to his family or a neutral doctor. He has an eye condition which was neglected for months and has meant he’s probably almost lost sight in one eye.” Late last month, Sky Sports aired an interview with Khasim and Sulaiman during its coverage of a test match between England and Pakistan. The Pakistan Cricket Board, which has close links to the government and whose chair is also the interior minister, made a formal complaint to Sky Sports after the broadcast and the Pakistani team threatened to refuse to return to the field after the lunch break. “It shows how out of touch they are with the rest of the world, that they thought they could silence media like they do at home,” Sulaiman said of the complaint. “It just exposed them for the authoritarian regime that they are.” The UN has said Khan’s prolonged detention violates international law and the UN’s special rapporteur on torture said his solitary confinement and detention conditions could amount to psychological torture. Sulaiman said the family had been told their father, 73, had also been diagnosed with high blood pressure. “More than anything, we just want to speak to him and make sure he’s OK,” he said. Khan’s sons said they were particularly concerned that the “cruel” treatment was being driven by a “personal grudge” by Asim Munir, Pakistan’s chief of defence forces and army chief. View image in fullscreen Asim Munir praying after laying a wreath on the martyrs’ monument during a ceremony in Rawalpindi last year. Photograph: AP When Khan was the prime minister, he unceremoniously demoted Munir, and the bad blood between them was well known . When Munir was made army chief in 2022, the persecution of Khan increased notably. “It’s very clear this is being driven by personal grudge and that’s one of the reasons he’s being treated so harshly, on the orders of Asim Munir,” said Sulaiman. Munir’s powers expanded over the past year as he established himself as a close ally of Donald Trump, who referred to him as “my favourite field marshal”. Last month, the supreme court ruled that Khan should be taken to a private hospital for treatment for a blood clot in his retinal vein, believed to have destroyed 85% of the sight in his right eye because of a prolonged lack of medical attention. Khan was instead taken briefly to a government hospital, where he was given several injections and ruled fit to return to prison, prompting outrage from his family and political party. “There’s still been no light shed on our father’s real condition from an unbiased, neutral physician,” said Kasim. “We believe they’re trying to slowly kill him in there. Just as soon as there’s less pressure, we are sure they will put even harsher restrictions on him and try to finish him off. “The one with the real vendetta here is the army chief Asim Munir.” Prisoner number 804: the plot to erase Imran Khan – podcast Read more In a statement, the Pakistan government called the allegations around Khan “fake propaganda” and said he was being kept in adequate conditions, with access to home-cooked food, nuts, bottled water, exercise equipment, family visits and regular medical examinations. “The government of Pakistan categorically rejects allegations that the convicted prisoner is being subjected to punitive solitary confinement, cruelty or deprivation,” the statement said. It was widely acknowledged that Khan came to power in 2018 with the backing of Pakistan’s military, widely referred to as the “establishment”, which has long held an oversized role in the country’s governance. Khan had promised to build a “naya Pakistan” (new Pakistan), which would end corruption and follow the rule of law. However, his time in power was plagued by allegations of corruption, press censorship and persecution of his opponents. He was toppled in 2022 after falling out with his military benefactors. He then began a campaign calling for the generals to be kept out of government. By 2023, as his accusations against the military grew, Khan turned from alleged persecutor to the persecuted . He was arrested and charged with more than 100 crimes, including alleged corruption and sedition, which he claims are trumped up to keep him out of power. Despite his toppling and imprisonment, Khan still remains popular. “They want to do everything they can to sideline him and disappear him from public life,” Kasim said. View image in fullscreen Supporters of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf display a poster of Imran Khan at a rally in February on the second anniversary of the 2024 general elections, which the party alleges were rigged. Photograph: Bilawal Arbab/EPA Sulaiman said that while it was “clear the establishment think they can get away with it without any kind of repercussions”, it was also evident the government had been rattled by international coverage of Khan’s case. Khan’s sons said that while they were keen to travel to Pakistan, their visas had still not been granted more than nine months after applying. They emphasised they had no interest in entering politics in Pakistan or leading Khan’s PTI party in his absence. “We definitely don’t want to get involved in politics in Pakistan in the long term,” said Sulaiman. “Our father always said that one of the biggest problems with Pakistani politics is this dynastic nepotism; that power’s been held by just two families for the last 40 years. It’s a sign of what’s wrong with the political system in Pakistan.” Speculation has abounded on whether Khan would strike a deal with the military to secure his release. Khan’s closest aide, Zulfi Bukhari, said: “There is only one deal Khan would ever accept: the restoration of democracy, the rule of law and the people’s mandate in Pakistan. If they’re genuinely willing to do that, then fine – let’s talk.” Kasim and Sulaiman said they did not believe Khan would give up his politics to secure his release. “He’s a very single-minded person,” said Kasim. “I don’t think there’s a chance that he’d ever give it up.” Explore more on these topics Imran Khan Pakistan South and central Asia Solitary confinement news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Pakistan complain to Sky after interview with Imran Khan’s sons over father’s treatment Jailed ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan allowed brief hospital visit after uproar over health Prisoner number 804: the plot to erase Imran Khan Imran Khan’s health in ‘grave danger’ after eye blockage diagnosis, party says Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan sentenced to 14 years in prison in corruption case Who is Bushra Bibi? https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/10/17/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter: Zelenszkij azt kérte, hogy Magyarországon keresztül is szállíthassanak kukoricát Nyugat-Európába Külföld Aradi Hanga Zsófia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Volodimir Zelenszkij a pénteki EU-csúcs plenáris ülésén jelezte, hogy jelenleg a Fekete-tengeren nem lehetséges a gabonaszállítás, és azt kérte Lengyelországtól, Romániától, Szlovákiától és Magyarországtól, hogy mint a háború elején, úgy most is engedjék, hogy a területükön át szállítson gabonát Ukrajna a nyugati országokba – mondta Magyar Péter az RTL-nek a brüsszeli csúcsról hazafelé tartva pénteken. A miniszterelnök a csatornának azt mondta, erre volt egy jól bejáratott eljárás 3-4 éve, ami megszűnt. Az ukrán elnök a négyszemközti megbeszélésükön is említette, hogy nagy segítség lenne, ha leplombálva, vonatokkal át tudnák szállítani Nyugat-Európába a kukoricát. „Mondtam, hogy amennyiben ez csak átmegy az országon, akkor nyilván ennek nincsen akadálya” – mondta Magyar. Arról, hogy miről esett még szó az ukrán elnök és a magyar miniszterelnök közötti tárgyaláson, ebben a cikkben írtunk . Magyar az RTL-nek annyit mondott, rövid, alig negyed órás megbeszélés volt, aminek a végén abban maradtak, miniszteri szinteken folytatódnak a megbeszélések, és találnak olyan projekteket, akár iskola- vagy kórházfelújítást, vagy gazdasági befektetést Kárpátalján, amit végig tudnak vinni. „Pár hónap múlva, ha jól haladnak a tárgyalások, a kisebbségi megállapodás végrehajtása, akkor találkozunk.” Ahogy arról nyáron részletesen is írtunk, az ukránok egyre fokozódó, az orosz olajinfrastruktúra ellen végrehajtott hatékony támadásaira Moszkva olyan választ talált, amivel nemcsak az ukránoknak, hanem a világ ellátási láncai közül egy újabbnak okozhat jelentős károkat: sorozatos támadásokkal fojtófogásba vette az ukrán fekete-tengeri gabonaszállítást . A fekete-tengeri helyzet azért okozhat világszerte érezhető problémát, mert 2022-höz hasonlóan épp a leginkább élénk időszakban állhat le ismét a gabonaexport Ukrajnából. A megtámadott ország még most is a világ kilencedik legnagyobb gabonaexportőre, 3 százalékos globális részesedéssel. 2026 első felében ezek az ukrán kikötők még a háború ellenére is több mint 42 millió tonna árut kezeltek. 2022-ben, az orosz–ukrán háború elején ezért is született viszonylag gyorsan megoldás: török közvetítéssel sikerült elérni, hogy az oroszok kötelezettséget vállaljanak arra, hogy meghatározott folyosón belül nem akadályozzák az ukrán gabona tengeri szállítását. Ez az elmúlt években, ha nem is mindig akadálytalanul, de működött, egészen idén nyárig. Kapcsolódó Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Kövess minket Facebookon is! https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: ‘Door-camera videos show footage of residents screaming when the coyote approached and the animal chasing a cat up a tree.’ Photograph: Natural History Library/Alamy View image in fullscreen ‘Door-camera videos show footage of residents screaming when the coyote approached and the animal chasing a cat up a tree.’ Photograph: Natural History Library/Alamy Los Angeles Residents fear wild coyote becoming too comfortable in LA neighborhood A coyote, that has reportedly been roaming the trendy Atwater Village for months, attacked a one-year-old boy Dara Kerr Tue 20 Oct 2026 12.00 EDT Last modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 12.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google One Los Angeles neighborhood has been at war over a wild coyote, and over the weekend it all came to a head. For months, the animal had been roaming the trendy Atwater Village, showing up in broad daylight, sleeping in back yards and approaching residents. At least one person had reportedly fed the coyote and others affectionately nicknamed it Wiley. But some residents feared the creature had become dangerously too cozy. On Friday evening, the coyote entered a family’s back yard and attacked a 16-month-old boy. When the boy and his mother fled to their house, the animal followed them inside and was reluctant to leave, according to local news station KTLA . The child was treated at a hospital and discharged. “A coyote was seen at the location where the incident occurred, and it was euthanized,” the California department of fish and wildlife told KTLA, adding that DNA samples were collected from both the boy and the coyote. “The samples will be analyzed to determine if the coyote that was taken is the offending animal.” If it was the same coyote, this wasn’t its first time showing aggressive behavior. Apparently, the animal had a track record of stalking people in the neighborhood. Door-camera videos showed footage of residents screaming when the coyote approached and the animal chasing a cat up a tree, according to KTLA. When a local public radio station posted a story on Instagram in August titled “Is Wiley welcome in your neighborhood?”, commenters were torn. One person wrote: “I live here; I say he stays. It’s as much his home as anyone else’s.” While another cautioned: “We gotta stay vigilant tho lmfao. Homie be casually prowling in the driveway.” Rebecca Dmytryk, who lives in Atwater Village and is the CEO of Humane Wildlife Control, told the Los Angeles Times that she filed a complaint in July to fish and wildlife asking that the agency speak with the man who was reportedly feeding the coyote, but she didn’t hear back. “Single coyote reported loitering and hanging out in the person’s backyard sleeping on top of vehicle,” read Dmytryk’s complaint, according to the Los Angeles Times. “Coyote reportedly following people as they will do when they are human conditioned, associating humans with handouts.” Other residents also filed complaints with the city and state, but say no action was taken. A spokesperson for fish and wildlife told the Los Angeles Times that the agency followed up on tips it received and is investigating the allegations of feeding the coyote. “This situation required intervention long before a child was injured,” Dmytryk told the newspaper. “Now a child has been hurt, and a coyote is dead.” The California department of fish and wildlife did not immediately return a request for comment.
